title: Rum Punch
subtitle: Classic Caribbean rum punch
excerpt: Caribbean rum punch follows a simple rhyme: one of sour, two of sweet, three of strong, four of weak. Lime juice, sugar, dark rum, and fruit juice in those proportions make the ideal punch. It is the drink of the Caribbean -- made at every gathering from Jamaica to Barbados.
sourceNotes: The rum punch formula -- one sour, two sweet, three strong, four weak -- has been used across the Caribbean for centuries. It appears in a Barbadian proverb from the 18th century. Rum is the spirit of the Caribbean, produced on nearly every island from fermented sugarcane molasses.

recipe.batchNotes: Scale up using the same proportions. Makes a large batch for a party easily.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 24 hours ahead and keep refrigerated without ice. Add ice just before serving.

content.text: The proportions are the key. Use freshly squeezed lime juice -- not bottled. Dark rum gives the best flavour. Angostura bitters is a Trinidadian product and a classic addition -- a few dashes transforms the punch. Serve over lots of ice.

items.prepNote: use juice of 2 limes plus 100ml dark rum (this is the rum)
juice only -- use fresh orange or a mix of orange and pineapple juice
use simple syrup (equal parts sugar and water, stirred until dissolved)
a pinch of nutmeg and a few drops of Angostura bitters are traditional garnishes

content.text: Make the simple syrup: stir 100g sugar into 100ml warm water until fully dissolved. Cool.
Squeeze the limes -- you need about 100ml of juice. Measure out the rum.
Combine the lime juice, sugar syrup, rum, and orange or fruit juice in a large jug or punch bowl. Stir well.
Taste. Adjust the lime or sugar to your preference. Add a pinch of grated nutmeg.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Pour over ice into glasses. Add a dash of Angostura bitters and a slice of orange or lime to each glass.

items.symptom: Punch is too sharp and sour
items.cause: Limes were very acidic or too much lime juice was used
items.fix: Add more simple syrup a tablespoon at a time and stir and taste after each addition

items.cause: The fruit juice added a lot of natural sugar alongside the syrup
items.fix: Add more lime juice in small amounts to bring the acidity back into balance

items.cause: Watered down by too much ice
items.fix: Keep the punch in the fridge rather than over ice; add ice only to the glasses immediately before serving

content.text: Rum punch is the drink of the entire Caribbean. Every island has its version, from Bajan rum punch in Barbados to ti-punch in Martinique. The rhyme -- one of sour, two of sweet, three of strong, four of weak -- has been the guide since at least the 18th century. Rum itself is made from sugarcane, which was the crop that defined Caribbean history for three hundred years.
